entries.title: College acceptance + ML/LLM skill base
entries.comment: Got into an Electrical Engineering program — a real milestone, even coming to it a bit later than typical. Built genuine technical footing this period: basic grasp of core ML algorithms (linear/logistic regression), got LLMs running locally, and shipped a working BitNet inference wrapper. Also in a casual relationship that's taking some pressure off day to day, which helped rather than hurt everything else.

entries.title: Built BitNet inference wrapper
entries.comment: Built a working, lightweight inference wrapper for Microsoft's experimental BitNet architecture. A concrete shipped artifact, not just tinkering — real forward movement on the technical skill side.

entries.title: Learned ML fundamentals
entries.comment: Picked up basic working knowledge of core ML algorithms — linear and logistic regression. Foundational rather than a big leap, but real groundwork that everything after builds on.

entries.title: Got into Electrical Engineering program
entries.comment: Accepted into an Electrical Engineering program — a genuine milestone, arriving a bit later than typical but no less real for it.

entries.title: New relationship easing stress
entries.comment: In a casual, not especially serious relationship that's been a genuine relief on the mental-stress side of things.

entries.title: Didn't get into CIS
entries.comment: Rejected from the CIS program — a real setback at the time. In hindsight it's part of the same arc, since the EE acceptance followed a month later, but it stung on its own and belongs in the record as the dip before the recovery.
